name: University Archives
blurb: Official records documenting the history and administration of the University of Melbourne since its founding in 1853.
location: Baillieu Library, The University of Melbourne, Parkville VIC 3010

sub_collections.name: Governance Records
sub_collections.blurb: Council minutes, by-laws, statutes and committee papers from 1853 onwards.

sub_collections.name: Student Records
sub_collections.blurb: Enrolment registers, graduation lists, student files and academic records (subject to access conditions).

sub_collections.name: Buildings & Campus
sub_collections.blurb: Architectural drawings, campus plans, building permits and records relating to the University's physical estate.

sub_collections.name: Official Correspondence
sub_collections.blurb: Incoming and outgoing correspondence of the Vice-Chancellor, Council and administrative departments.

sub_collections.name: Photographic Records
sub_collections.blurb: Official and informal photographs documenting campus life, events, staff, students and buildings over time.

sub_collections.name: Publications & Reports
sub_collections.blurb: Annual reports, calendars, gazettes, prospectuses and other official University publications.

name: Rare Books & Special Collections
blurb: Rare printed works, manuscripts, incunabula and illuminated texts from the Baillieu Library's Special Collections.

name: Personal Papers Collection
blurb: Papers, correspondence and personal records donated by academics, researchers and notable figures.

name: Maps, Plans & Architectural Drawings
blurb: Historical maps, architectural plans, survey charts and drawings documenting places, buildings and campuses.

name: Anthropology Museum
blurb: Ethnographic and archaeological objects from cultures worldwide, including significant Australian collections.
holding: School of Social and Political Sciences

name: Zoology Museum
blurb: Natural history specimens including vertebrates, invertebrates, and comparative anatomy collections.

name: Medical History Museum
blurb: Historical medical instruments, teaching models, pathological specimens and records documenting medical education.
about: Explore, inquire and enjoy the social history of medicine and its role in society through a diverse exhibition program. Visit the nineteenth century Savory and Moore Pharmacy complete with pharmaceutical jars and equipment. The Medical History Museum is a free museum for those inquisitive about medicine's contribution to scientific discovery and community well being.
holding: Faculty of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences

name: Henry Forman Atkinson Dental Museum
blurb: Instruments, equipment and teaching materials documenting the history of dentistry and oral health education.
about: Visit the Henry Forman Atkinson Dental Museum to be inspired by the intriguing history of dental health and the development of the dental professions and dental education. It is the oldest and most significant dental collection in Australia, tracing its origins back to 1884 with the formation of the Odontological Society of Victoria, the organisation responsible for establishing the first dental school in Victoria.

name: Harry Brookes Allen Museum of Anatomy and Pathology
blurb: Anatomical and pathological specimens, models and teaching collections supporting medical education and research.
about: The Harry Brookes Allen Museum of Anatomy and Pathology is one of Australia's largest collections of human tissue specimens, animal anatomy specimens and historical anatomical models, offering students and researchers a unique insight into the human body. Although the museum is not normally open to the public, tours of the museum are available for biology and medical professionals and students.

name: FEIT
blurb: Records, instruments and teaching collections from the Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology.
about: The collection documents the history of teaching and research in engineering and information technology at the University of Melbourne from 1861 to the present. The collection comprises over 4,500 objects and images and related archives, demonstrating the contributions of the University to technological, economic and social development.
holding: Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology

name: Geology Museum
blurb: Mineralogy, petrology and palaeontology specimens including significant geological samples from across Australia.
holding: School of Geography, Earth and Atmospheric Sciences

name: University Herbarium
blurb: Pressed plant specimens from the 19th century onwards, including rare and endemic species from across Australia.

name: Law Museum
blurb: Historic legal instruments, court records, archival documents and artefacts relating to the history of law.

name: University Art Collection
blurb: A major university art collection featuring Australian and international works spanning painting, sculpture and works on paper.
about: The University of Melbourne Art Collection is the largest university-based art collection in Australia, comprising over 18,000 artworks. The collection includes major holdings of paintings, prints and drawings, ceramics and sculpture, including contemporary Australian art and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art.

name: Prints, Drawings & Watercolours
blurb: Original prints, drawings, watercolours and works on paper from the 18th to 21st centuries from Australia and abroad.

name: Indigenous Australian Art Collection
blurb: Works by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists spanning bark paintings, acrylic works, fibre art and more.

name: Photographic & Pictorial Collection
blurb: Historical photographs, glass plate negatives, lantern slides and pictorial records from the 19th century onwards.

name: Audio-Visual Archive
blurb: Film, video and sound recordings including ethnographic recordings, oral histories and historical footage.

name: Ephemera & Printed Images
blurb: Printed ephemera including postcards, broadsides, posters and illustrated printed material from across the collections.

name: Grainger Museum Collection
blurb: The personal collection of composer Percy Grainger including instruments, manuscripts, correspondence and experimental machines.
about: Australian musician and composer Percy Grainger established the Grainger Museum in 1938, motivated by the desire to interpret and contextualise his creative achievements and cultural environment. The Grainger Museum Collection, an internationally significant archive of over 100,000 items, spans a range of disciplines, from experimental sound technology and musical instruments to costumes, ethnography, art and design. The collection is brought to life through collaboration with students, academic partners and artists and their creative work and production.

name: The Ed Muirhead Physics Museum
blurb: Historic optical and measurement instruments from the University of Melbourne's School of Physics.
about: The Ed Muirhead Physics Museum holds instruments used in physics teaching and research at the University of Melbourne, including microscopes, spectrographs and pyrometers dating from the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
